local_checks.invariant: Agent tool calls run on a dedicated pool separate from human API threads, and per-sandbox tool_concurrency bounds how many pool threads one sandbox can hold
local_checks.result: api.py:81 creates a 32-thread tool_pool used only by POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool} (api.py:206-211). service.py:274-278 enforces 4 concurrent calls per sandbox (429 beyond) and decrements in finally (288-290). One sandbox can hold at most 4 of 32 pool threads; saturating the pool takes 8 or more sandboxes acting together (aggregate, not a single-principal bypass). Approved actions run on the human request thread (service.py:414-415, Starlette threadpool), and exec there is bounded by timeout -k 5 exec_timeout (sandbox.py:531).

local_checks.invariant: Work done on behalf of sandbox B is charged to B's tool_concurrency and never runs on another sandbox's or a human's request thread
local_checks.result: Mocked harness in sbx: with an idle open GUI burst for sbB, sbA's call_tool('list_dir') ran sbB's workspace_manifest on sbA's thread (manifest calls [('sbB','sbA-request')], elapsed 0.50s = stub delay) while _busy only shows sbA. expire_stale() (reached from GET/POST approvals and decide) ran the same sbB close on the human thread (0.50s). service.py:273 calls close_idle_gui_bursts() before the busy check, and it iterates every sandbox's bursts (service.py:250-256).

local_checks.invariant: Every docker exec reached from the burst-close and GUI paths has a deadline
local_checks.result: Of the execs, only exec (sandbox.py:531), read_file (561) and outbox_read (665) carry a timeout. workspace_manifest (499), desktop_processes ps and xdotool (689-691), kill_processes (697), and the _x GUI calls (683-684, used by click/type/key/screenshot/geometry) use exec_run with no timeout, and the docker SDK exec_run has no deadline parameter. Whether container state can actually keep these execs from returning is runtime behaviour, not visible in source.

x_hardening: tool_pool (32) / tool_concurrency (4) means 8 or more cooperating sandboxes can occupy every tool thread for up to exec_timeout+5 s per call; human routes run on the separate Starlette pool, so the effect is limited to other agents' tool latency. Consider a global cap tied to the pool size or a fair queue.

Client disconnect does not cancel tool_pool work (api.py:209 run_in_executor); bounded for exec by its timeout, but the untimed execs listed above have no such bound. Add a deadline to every container exec (e.g. wrap in timeout as exec does).

snapshot_quota counts human manual and import snapshots toward the agent's quota (sandbox.py:503-505 counts all rows). That is conservative, but it can push an agent into approval mode earlier than the operator expects.
